findings.title: Retention check uses wrong comparison
findings.body: The check `days < MIN_RETENTION_DAYS` rejects valid retention periods equal to `MIN_RETENTION_DAYS`, which should be allowed. Change to `days <= MIN_RETENTION_DAYS` to permit the minimum retention period.
findings.suggestion:
if days <= MIN_RETENTION_DAYS:
        raise ValueError(f"retention below {MIN_RETENTION_DAYS} days is not allowed")

findings.title: Missing increment of removed count
findings.body: The loop deletes files but never increments `removed`, so the function always returns 0 even when files are deleted. Increment `removed` inside the loop to return the actual count.

findings.title: Nightly cleanup uses too short retention
findings.body: The cleanup calls `purge_older_than(ttl_days)` with `ttl_days = 7`, which is below the minimum retention of 30 days enforced in `retention.py`. Either raise the TTL to 30 or remove the minimum check if 7 days is intentional.

summary.problem: Retention logic rejects the minimum allowed period and the nightly cleanup uses a too-short TTL, and the purge function does not count removed files.
summary.done_well: A minimum retention policy is introduced and enforced, and the storage interface is used correctly.
